precepts.text: The word, the Commandments, is the lamp and light David means in verse 1; the Most High gave us the Commandments as instructions to walk through this captivity.
precepts.point: Even with everything coming against us today, covid-19, the vaccine, all the different things being pushed, wars going on, these words remind us that in this we can be confident. Whether it is other camps, family, or other nations coming against us, we can still be confident.

note.label: Psalm 27: The Most High Is My Light and Salvation

precepts.why:
“The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” The light David means is the word: “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.”

The word, the Commandments, is the lamp and the light of verse 1. The Most High is David's guide and his way to salvation, and He gave us the Commandments as instructions to walk through this captivity. It is a rhetorical question: if the Most High is my salvation, why should I be afraid of anybody?

note.label: Psalm 27: The Most High Is My Light and Salvation

precepts.why:
“Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.” Psalm 91 carries the same thought: “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

He that dwells in the secret place of the Most High is under the shadow of the Almighty, his refuge and fortress. This is very good reading for what is going on in these last days. With everything coming against us today, covid-19, the vaccine, all the different things being pushed, wars going on, whether it is other camps, family, or other nations coming against us, in this we can still be confident. The wicked that come to eat up our flesh stumble and fall.

precepts.point: This is just one instance; there are many scenarios where the Most High will encamp around you and be your refuge, even when people come against IUIC He is there in the midst.

note.label: Psalm 27: The Most High Is My Light and Salvation

precepts.why:
“For in the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion: in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me”. Lord willing, much of Israel alive will have to go through this time of trouble, and He says He will hide you. Psalm 91 lays out that hiding: “Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence. He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.”

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday. A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.” A thousand fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, but it does not come near you.

“Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked. Because thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation”. Only with your eyes will you behold the reward of the wicked when Christ returns, because you made the Most High your habitation. This is just one instance; there are many scenarios where the Most High will encamp around you and be your refuge, even when people come against IUIC, He is there in the midst.

note.label: Psalm 27: The Most High Is My Light and Salvation

precepts.why:
“When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up.” Christ warned it would come to that: “Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”

Your enemies will be those of your own household. Close family can be the ones that forsake you and come against you in these last days. When father and mother forsake you, the Most High takes you up; He has been our help, and He will not leave us nor forsake us.

precepts.text: Believe in Him and He will help you; stipulations to His help. The fearful heart and the sinner that goeth two ways cannot serve both; the fainthearted who believes not shall not be defended.
precepts.point: Wait on the Most High and be of good courage, and He shall strengthen your heart. But the double-minded, half in and half out, He will not defend, and this comes up again in the later chapters.

note.label: Psalm 27: The Most High Is My Light and Salvation

precepts.why:
“I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living. Wait on the Lord: be of good courage”. Every line reads like a stipulation, and Ecclesiasticus lays the stipulations out: “Believe in him, and he will help thee; order thy way aright, and trust in him. Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall. Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail.”

Believe in Him and He will help you; those are stipulations to His help. “Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?” Without faith that the kingdom is coming, David would have fainted, but he believed to see the goodness of the Lord.

Then the warning: “Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goeth two ways! Woe unto him that is fainthearted! for he believeth not; therefore shall he not be defended.” The fearful heart and the sinner that goeth two ways cannot serve both. The double-minded, half in and half out, He will not defend, and this comes up again in the later chapters. Wait on the Most High, be of good courage, and He shall strengthen your heart, even with false witnesses and such as breathe out cruelty risen up against you.

moments.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up. That is a heavy verse right there.

Write this down: forsake means either death, or that they are at a distance from you, unable to help in time of need. They may not have the finances. They may be unkind to you. They may be unmindful of you, meaning inconsiderate — they do not notice. Some parents are like that. When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up. The Lord will deal with you.
Some of you may not have functioning parents in your lives. There is such a thing as elders in your lives — what you call your OGs today on the street.
